comments_text: Discovery: it is hypothesized that Glycosaminoglycan (GAG)-binding proteins could also recognize LPS and enclose cryptic antibiotic motifs. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (42.11%) to Engraulisin. H=R: 17%, V=L=T: 11%. Mol Wt: 2269.7. Activity: Active against E. coli (MIC 1.6 uM), A. baumannii (MIC 1.6 uM), Pseudomonas sp (MIC 3.1 uM), S. aureus (MIC 50 uM), E.faecium (MIC >100 uM), and L. monocytogenes (MIC 6.3 uM). MOA:bacteria:E. coli: permeated bacterial membranes and depolarized bacterial membranes. The peptide also binds to LPS.
reference_text: Mol Syst Biol. 2025 May 23. doi: 10.1038/s44320-025-00120-6. PubMed

comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (86.96%) to synthetic NLF20.L: 17%; F: 13%, R: 22%. Mol Wt: 2932.4. Activity: Active against E. coli (MIC 0.4 uM), A. baumannii ATCC 15308 (MIC 0.2 uM), Pseudomonas sp (MIC 0.8 uM), S. aureus (MIC 6.3 uM), E. faecium (MIC 3.1 uM), and L. monocytogenes (MIC 1.6 uM). MOA:bacteria:E. coli: permeated bacterial membranes and depolarized bacterial membranes. The peptide also binds to LPS. Structure: CD: random coil in PBS, and helical after binding to 10 mM SDS, 50 ug/ml LPS, or 20 ug/ml heparin. NMR study: chemcial shift diffrences indicate residues 3-15 are helical bound to DPC. Peptide stability: half-life in vitro:serum:human (50%): t1/2 48.9 min (cf.: the D-form: t1/2 >360 min). In vitro toxicity: horse RBC: 23% hemolysis at 250 uM. Cytotoxicity: MRC-5 (TC50 69 uM). Animal model:mouse: BALB/c, bacterial sepsis:A. baumannii, i.p./i.p. x3 (treated 3 times 2 hpi at 20 mg/kg), CFU reduced 1-2 logs in liver, spleen, lung, and kidney. Peptide engineering:dHBP-5 (peptide made in D-amino acids): the L and D-forms HBP-5 peptides showed similar efficacy in different organs in the case of female mice. The efficacy, however, is slightly better for the D-form in the case of male mice. The D-form appeared to be more active (lower MIC values) (D>L).
reference_text: Mol Syst Biol. 2025 May 23. doi: 10.1038/s44320-025-00120-6. PubMed

comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (90.48%) to synthetic NLF20.L: 20%; F: 15%, R: 20%. Activity: Active against E. coli (MIC 0.4 uM), A. baumannii ATCC 15308 (MIC 0.4 uM), Pseudomonas sp (MIC 0.4 uM), S. aureus (MIC 6.3 uM), and L. monocytogenes (MIC 1.6 uM). Structure: CD: random coil in PBS, and helical after binding to 50 ug/ml LPS only. Peptide stability: half-life in vitro:serum:human (50%): t1/2 88.5 min. In vitro toxicity: horse RBC: 24% hemolysis at 250 uM. Cytotoxicity: MRC-5 (TC50 63 uM). Animal model:mouse: BALB/c, bacterial sepsis:A. baumannii, i.p./i.p. x3 (treated 3 times 2 hpi at 20 mg/kg), CFU reduced 2-3 logs in liver, spleen, lung, and kidney. Interestingly, the bacterium was cleared better in female mice for this shortened peptide in all the organs (CFU drop by ~ 4 logs).
reference_text: Mol Syst Biol. 2025 May 23. doi: 10.1038/s44320-025-00120-6. PubMed
